To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the neutral lipid to polar lipid ratio, a proxy for the lipid storage, is related to the individual body weight in dominant Baltic zooplankton taxa and this relationship is the strongest and the only significant across different species and development stages.

the lipid storage capacity in dominant Baltic copepodes and cladoceran species increases with individual body size and that body weight is the most significant predictor for lipid storage capacity in zooplankters.
individual body weight was the strongest and most significant predictor of NL/PL ratio, a proxy for lipid content, across different developmental stages and species in the Baltic Sea.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between body size and lipid content in zooplanktivorous organisms and its applicability in the context of zooplanktivory.
the use of body size as a trait reflecting nutritional properties of zooplanktivorous prey.
a relationship between individual body size and lipid storage in dominant zooplankton species of the Baltic Sea.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lipid storage capacity of a zooplantkon community can be estimated by using the mean body weight of zooplankters.
the NL/PL-ratio is a good indicator of lipid storage capacity, and that body weight is a good predictor of NL/PL-ratios.
the lipid storage capacity of the dominant Baltic copepoids and cladoceran species is positively related to their size, and the relationship is similar across species, stages and sexes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the size structure of the zooplankton assemblage can be used as an indicator for nutritional quality of zooplkankton prey.
lipid storage capacity of Baltic Sea zooplanton is positively related to body size, but the relationship varies among species.
the size structure of a community is a good predictor of the nutritional quality of the prey.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NL/PL lipid ratio can be estimated using only the mean body size of the zooplankton, which can be measured in the field.

the size structure of zooplankters is a good indicator of their nutritional quality, and thus the size structure of the zooplankton can be a useful tool for evaluating trophic conditions in marine ecosystems.

the NL/PL lipid ratio is not an appropriate proxy for the nutritional quality of copepod and cladoceran prey for Baltic Sea zooplantivorous fish, because the NL/PL ratios of different zooplankton species and developmental stages are not significantly different from each other.
